sentences.text:
Rangilal vs The State Of U.P. Thru. Its Prin. Secy. ... on 17
January, 2024
Author: Pankaj Bhatia

Bench: Pankaj Bhatia
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:4856
Court No. - 12
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 14006 of 2023
Applicant :- Rangilal

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- The State Of U.P. Thru.
Its Prin. Secy. Home Deptt., Lko.

And Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Shiv Pal Singh,Ambrish Kumar

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. No one appears on behalf of the respondent no.2 despite service of notice.
3.
In terms of the F.I.R., initially a missing person report was lodged alleging that the applicant had enticed away the victim.

In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim disclosed her age as 17 years and stated that she was talking with the applicant for the last one year and as her family members refused to marry her with the applicant, she went with the applicant and stayed with the applicant and later on came home.
In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she admitted that the applicant wanted to marry her which which was refused by her.
She also admitted that she used to talk with the applicant.
Medical on record, indicates the tentative age of the victim as 15 years.

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail by arguing that the age of the victim is less than 18 years.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant further argued that as there is no definite document on record prescribed under the Juvenile Justice Act and the rules framed thereunder to form a view with regard to age determination of the victim, as such the same would be decided at the time of trial in view of the law laid down in the case of Monish Vs. State of U.P. passed by this Court in Crl. Misc.
Bail Application No.55026 of 2021 decided on 9.2.2023.

entities.text:
Crl. Misc.
Bail Application No.55026 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant has no criminal history and is in jail since 18.4.2023, hence the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

6. Considering the fact that the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
do not corroborate the prosecution story

; the applicant has no criminal history and is languishing in jail since 18.4.2023; the age of the victim is to be determined at the time of the trial in view of the law laid down in the case of Monish Vs. State of U.P.(supra) as well as in terms of the Juvenile Justice Act and the rules framed thereunder, and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Rangilal be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.149 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Malhipur, District Shrawasti on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 17.1.2024/
